packet.claim: recover_json_object ignores fenced candidates when there is more than one code fence, so it can score a later non-fenced object instead of the last fenced object as documented.
packet.expected: The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one; for the reproducer, that is {"b": 2}.
packet.observed: The code only uses the fenced pool when len(fenced) == 1; with two fences it falls through to top_level and returns the last top-level object, {"c": 3}.
packet.scope: replies containing two or more fenced JSON objects and a later top-level JSON object outside any fence
packet.source_basis: The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text
packet.uncertainty: The phrase 'any fence holds one' could be read as 'exactly one fence', but the surrounding text and contrast with 'else the last top-level object' indicate at least one fence.
